thread:
maria - AE: FYI sent SentinelBank the PrivateDeploy POC checklist. They came back with a few blocking asks: static egress IPs for allowlisting, an exception for TLS inspection on a subset of backend FQDNs, and proof of how we preserve client identity for audit. Can SE/NetEng/Sec weigh in? @devon @raj @olivia :eyes:

devon - SE: Quick summary from the call — they will run a strict firewall whitelist (FQDN + IP) and cannot accept dynamic egress IPs from our side. They prefer PrivateLink for security but asked whether we can do an "SNI bump" so their inspection appliance sees client SNI while still terminating TLS on our side for features like streaming.

raj - NetEng: Short answer: SNI bump + PrivateLink is tricky. With AWS interface endpoints (PrivateLink) traffic terminates at our ENI; source IP becomes our connector subnet IPs, so original client IP is not preserved. Options: 1) Customer deploys an egress-proxy (reverse proxy in their VPC) that forwards original client IP via X-Forwarded-For to our service; 2) Use VPC peering/Transit with a NAT that preserves source IPs (but this exposes routing and is more ops-heavy); 3) If they insist on true client IP at backend, we recommend a small proxy appliance on their side to preserve audit info.

olivia - Security: For the TLS inspection ask — we cannot recommend customers terminate TLS and then re-encrypt to us in a way that breaks certificate pinning for our runtime. If they need TLS inspection for compliance, the typical approach is: allowlist our egress IPs and exempt specific internal FQDNs from inspection so TLS remains end-to-end. We need the following from them to sign off:
- List of FQDNs that will be inspected
- Threat model for exempted flows
- SIEM/Syslog endpoint for audit logs

devon - SE: To make this concrete, here's the minimal firewall snippet they can add to their perimeter to allow PrivateLink plus our egress pool. Replace <REGION_EGRESS> with the region we publish.

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood PrivateDeploy egress pool
ALLOW TCP 443 to 18.225.0.0/20  # redwood-egress-1 (example)
ALLOW TCP 443 to 54.187.0.0/16  # redwood-ingest (example)
# If using PrivateLink interface endpoint, allow the interface ENI IP range or VPCE prefix
ALLOW TCP 443 to vpce-xxx.amazonaws.com (resolve to VPCE IPs)
```

raj - NetEng: A few networking caveats to surface:
- MTU: if they're doing an onprem VPN/DirectConnect into our PrivateDeploy VPC, ask NetOps to allow 1500 -> 9001 MTU passthrough if they use jumbo frames; otherwise packet fragmentation can increase latency for streaming tokens.
- Keepalives: long streaming sessions need idle TCP timeouts tuned (we've seen corporate proxies drop idle streams at 60s).
- Health checks: if they deploy a proxy in front, ensure sticky sessions or the X-Stream-ID header to rehydrate KV caches for low-latency generation.

maria - AE: Pricing question from procurement — if they put a proxy in front vs. allow us static egress from our Dedicated fleet, is there a cost diff? devon?

devon - SE: Yes — choices:
- Customer-managed proxy: no additional Redwood infra cost but added customer ops.
- Redwood-managed static egress (Dedicated): we can allocate reserved NAT/egress IPs inside their region as part of a Dedicated offer; that adds a small monthly surcharge (reserved egress block + SLA). For estimation, tell procurement we charge for reserved capacity + static egress block on Dedicated. I'll follow up with numbers in the quote.

olivia - Security: Also need to complete the question on certificate/key management for the POC — will they require HSM-backed keys on our side? If so, that changes timeline (we need an enterprise contract addendum).

maria - AE: They want to run a mini-PoC next week (3-day window). Action items:
- devon: prepare two network runbooks (PrivateLink + customer-proxy option) and a short pricing appendix for reserved egress.
- raj: add firewall allowlist snippet w/region IPs and note on MTU/keepalives.
- olivia: prepare a one-page security sign-off checklist and list of required fields for the security questionnaire.

devon - SE: Will do. I'll attach the runbooks and the quote stub here before EOD tomorrow. :+1:

raj - NetEng: Also pinging ops: if we provide reserved egress IPs, we need a /29 mapping per customer per region. Ops: can we pre-allocate a /29 for SentinelBank if they sign the commit?

deploy-bot: Deployment window reserved for Dedicated egress allocation: 2024-10-03 02:00-03:00 UTC (internal ticket #DGE-4592).

maria - AE: Great — thanks all. I'll update the customer and flag that we may need a quick legal addendum if Oliva requests HSM. Will loop back when devon posts the runbooks. :rocket:
